subject: Next steps: cost model & discount options for OrbitAI deployment
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@orbitai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today — rough budget & next steps

Hi Marcus / Monica,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to see Redwood's routing and caching approach. A few things we promised to share: our expected monthly token volume ranges and a target budget band for your pricing model.

Quick summary from our side:
- Primary workload: chat assistant + summarization for enterprise customers
- Expected Q3 average: 40M tokens/month (range 25M–60M)
- Spike capacity: up to 120M tokens in promotional periods
- Current internal target for cloud LLM spend: $1,200 — $1,800 / 1M tokens (we know that's a wide band)

We'd like to understand how startup discounts and committed-use/ multi-year incentives could move those unit rates down. Two asks from us:
1) Can you outline a starter discount for early-stage customers and what thresholds apply?
2) If we commit to a 12–24 month minimum with a modest pre-pay, what would a realistic $/1M token look like across bands (25M / 50M / 100M avg)?

I'm looping in procurement (procurement@orbitai.com) for timing — we may need an initial commercial ballpark to take internally next week.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Partnerships | OrbitAI

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 May 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — rough budget & next steps

Elena — thanks for the clear numbers and the context. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so procurement has something concrete to react to: 

Recap: 25M–60M steady, spikes up to 120M. Internal target $1.2k–$1.8k / 1M tokens.

What I'll put together this week:
- A simple pricing worksheet showing three commitment scenarios (starter, 1yr committed, 2yr committed) with per-1M token rates across your bands (25M / 50M / 100M).
- Startup program details (eligibility, founder credit, timing).
- Notes on how autoscaling/spikes are handled (burst buckets vs committed throughput) and how that affects unit economics.

One clarification that materially changes the math: are the 40M tokens/month a total across all users or per-product line (i.e., Chat vs Summaries)? If you can confirm distribution (approx % to chat vs summarization) I can better recommend quantization/ batching profiles that reduce cost.

I'll draft the worksheet and attach it as a shared Drive link plus a PDF summary for procurement. Can we aim to sync on Thursday (May 20) for a short 20-min pricing review?

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Procurement note: we have a $50k budget line available to commit in Q3 for infra spend if the unit economics get into the ~$800–$1,100 / 1M token area. If Redwood needs a signed commitment to get there, procurement can review 12–24 month commitments but needs to see simple math and payment terms.

Also asked: are there startup credits or founder discounts that can be applied while procurement finalizes the contract?

Happy to be on the 20th for the review — 10:00–10:30am PT works for us.

Elena

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@orbitai.com>, procurement@orbitai.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing worksheet & starter discount — OrbitAI proposal (draft)

Elena / Procurement / Team —

Per our sync, attached is the draft pricing workbook and a 1-page summary of the commitment options. High-level highlights (numbers in $ / 1M tokens):

- Starter (no-commit, startup program applied): 1,050 / 1M (applies for first 6 months or until a 12-month deal is signed; requires company < $10M ARR and founder confirmation)
- 12-mo committed (25M avg): 920 / 1M; 12-mo committed (50M avg): 770 / 1M
- 24-mo committed (50M avg): 640 / 1M; 24-mo committed (100M avg): 520 / 1M

Notes:
- The starter line assumes use of standard Redwood hosted runtime with prefix caching. If you move to a dedicated pool, unit rates improve but require minimum reserved capacity.
- Spikes: committed contracts include a 30% burst allowance above committed avg; excess beyond that billed at the committed rate + 40% surge fee. We can discuss a different spike model if you prefer a pure burst-bucket.
- Payments: quarterly in arrears is our default; we can do partial pre-pay discounts (shown in worksheet) if you want lower effective rates.

Attachments: OrbitAI_pricing_workbook.xlsx, commit_structure_summary.pdf

Next steps I recommend:
1) Procurement reviews the 1-pager and confirms which commitment(s) to model (12 vs 24 mo + pre-pay %).
2) If interested, we'll provision a formal quote and draft MSA with the relevant SLA appendix and billing schedule.
3) Monica will scope ramp/implementation milestones for the canary phase.

I can join procurement's internal call if that helps — happy to review numbers live. We've also included a HubSpot link with the draft deal record for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-ORB-2027-05

Thanks — looking forward to the quick follow-up.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing worksheet & starter discount — OrbitAI proposal (draft)

Quick tech note for procurement: the 65/35 chat-to-summary split is great — for the chat path we recommend enabling the KV cache and a 1k token context optimization which typically reduces cost by ~18% at steady-state compared to default. If OrbitAI expects a lot of long historical context per request we should model that separately since it changes effective tokens per session.

If procurement wants, we can run a 2-week profiling trial on your sample workload (ingest small set of chat logs) that will give a more precise $/1M estimate — there is no charge for the profiling itself (we only bill for production tokens once you go live).

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
